title: The Arians' selective quotation
english: The strange mid-chorus members of Arius's troupe say that Christ committed sin. But the words that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself (2 Corinthians 5:19) they neither hold in memory nor speak with the instruments of the tongue.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is describing how the Arians quote only part of a scriptural passage about Christ, saying he committed sin while omitting the words that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself.

title: The Arians as mutilating false accusers
english: But like clever false accusers and prosecutors, they mutilate the passage and then stage their contest of accusation.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius continues his accusation that the Arians quote Scripture dishonestly, now describing how they cut up the passage to make their case.

title: Lawful contenders must not mutilate; created and begotten exclude each other; what has a beginning admits corruption
english: Lawful contenders who love the truth must embrace all things without omission, not silence one part and tear away another part to present it for deception. For if Christ is created, then he is not begotten; and if he is begotten, then he is not created, since both categories cannot revolve around the same nature. Everything that has a beginning also admits an end, and everything that admits an end is capable of corruption.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is concluding his refutation of the Arians, first stating the rule for honest use of Scripture, then arguing that 'created' and 'begotten' cannot both apply to Christ, and finally that whatever has a beginning is capable of corruption.
